title: Men and women, side by side
hookLine: a verse naming believing men and women equally, ten qualities each, with one reward (33:35)
last: SOME WERE WIDOWS, SOME WERE MATCHES OF AFFECTION.

lines: THE ANSWER CAME AS A VERSE.
cards: A woman in Medina has been listening to the Qur'an for years. It's beautiful. It speaks to everyone.
But she has noticed something, and she says it out loud: why does it seem to address the men, and not mention us?
According to a report in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, it was Umm Salamah, one of the mothers of the believers, who asked. Other reports, one of them in Tirmidhi, name other women.
And the answer, the reports say, came as a verse.

teach.b: Pickthall begins it: "Lo! men who surrender unto Allah, and women who surrender, and men who believe and women who believe". And it keeps going, pair after pair, ten times. The devout men and women.
The truthful, the patient, the humble. The men and women who give in charity, who fast, who guard their chastity, who remember God much.
Then one ending for all of them: God has prepared for them forgiveness and a vast reward. In Arabic it sounds like a drumbeat: al-muslimina wal-muslimat, al-mu'minina wal-mu'minat.
The masculine plural, then the feminine, again and again. Arabic grammar normally lets the masculine plural cover everyone. This verse refuses the shortcut and names the women every single time.
Notice what the ten qualities are.

Not roles, not jobs: surrender, faith, devotion, truthfulness, patience, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, remembrance. The inner life, and the practices that shape it, each open to both and named for both.
One forgiveness, one vast reward. Muslims discuss many questions about men's and women's roles, and scholars and communities answer them differently.
This verse is one that people on many sides of those conversations quote, because on the things it lists, its answer is plain. Both, equally.

how: Muslims often cite 33:35 when teaching that men and women share the same spiritual duties and the same reward, and many learn its ten pairs of qualities by heart.

o: a Medina poet who praised the Prophet in verse
a mother of the believers who asked about women
the mother who set baby Musa on the river

games.q: men and women — tap the pairs.

s: the verse uses only the masculine plural to cover everyone
it names the women every time, ten times.
the reward in the verse is different for men and women
one forgiveness and one vast reward for all of them.
a report links the verse to a question from Umm Salamah
a report in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad says so; other reports name other women.

games.q: you're Umm Salamah. you've noticed the Qur'an seems to speak to the men. what do you do?
o: say nothing; it isn't your place.
ask the Prophet why women aren't mentioned.
games.why: a report in the Musnad of Imam Ahmad says she asked, and 33:35 came: men and women named side by side, ten times, with one reward.

practice: Go through the ten slowly: surrender, faith, devotion, truthfulness, patience, humility, charity, fasting, chastity, remembrance.

Which one do you see in someone of the other sex in your life, a sister, a brother, a colleague, a parent, a friend, and notice it's one you're trying to grow too. If you pray, you can pray for that person by name.

wordCard.voice: Umm Salamah, one of the mothers of the believers, whose question brought down this verse naming women by name, pair after pair. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: Muslim men and Muslim women, the first of the ten pairs in 33:35.

carryVoice: Your line: both, equally. Ten pairs, and a question that started it. Day five hundred forty-one, done.
